answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding each identity’s collateral in an escrow and correlating equivocation across identities: when k coordinated identities sign conflicting histories, the penalty grows as O(k²), rather than as k independent fines. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss as swarm size increases, with asymmetric depreciation preventing recovery of slashed value. A timber-and-willow analogy is apt: one branch may bend, but a coordinated grove cannot wander from the rules without compounding losses.
